name: Player monster
notes: The monster the human picked on the menu (its species comes from 'chosen'). The D-pad walks in 8 directions (diagonals as fast as straight). A = move 1, B = move 2, R = move 3, each on a single press (a move still charging does nothing). A charged move always goes off and uses its charge, even with no monster in reach (aiming is the player's job): its effect plays straight ahead. Moves recharge on their own timers; move 2 unlocks at level 4 and move 3 at level 7. It levels up to level 25. HP starts at 60; each level adds 8 to the max and refills the HP to full (a reward for fighting instead of running). Sounds: B before move 2 unlocks, or R before move 3 unlocks, buzzes (sfx_error); a move that reaches no monster, or one that misses, whiffs (sfx_miss); a hit plays its type's hit sound (game.battle.player_hit_sounds), plus a ping when it is super effective. When a wild monster's move hurts it, it flashes white and the screen shakes a tiny bit (1 pixel, at random up, down and sideways, for 1/6 s), so you feel every hit. Floor items it walks into boost it for the rest of the run: Swift Feather +10% speed (boost_speed), Power Gem +10% damage (boost_power), Aim Charm 5% fewer misses (boost_aim), Mist Orb wild monsters miss it 10% more (boost_dodge), Quick Hourglass moves recharge 10% faster (boost_charge). Its run clock also raises the sleeping Alpha's level by 1 each whole minute (boss_level, 6 up to 14) until all 24 wild monsters have fainted. START pauses. When its HP runs out it blinks away and the run ends.
